page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance hosted on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 16 dedicated virtual CPUs across 8 physical cores with 2 threads per core. The processor includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 35 MB of shared L3 cache, with hardware support for AVX and AVX-512 foundation instructions. The instance is configured with 32.0 GB of memory, maintaining a 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio at 2.0 GB per vCPU. No local storage is included, requiring all persistent disks to be network-attached, and the system offers a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps without bundled GPUs.

Benchmark results demonstrate modest single-thread capacity balanced against consistent multi-core throughput. Single-core tests such as Geekbench (930.0) and single-threaded gzip compression (19.07 GB/sec) place the instance in the lower tier of modern cloud compute benchmarks. However, multi-core metrics scale cleanly, yielding a Geekbench multi-core score of 5741.0, a PassMark CPU score of 13034.32, and software compilation benchmarks reaching 10524.0. Large-block memory bandwidth measures 75.27 GB/sec for reads and 55.21 GB/sec for writes, alongside a cached small-block read speed of 657.15 GB/sec.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the ecs.sn1ne.4xlarge provides accessible raw core density for parallel applications rather than per-core speed. The absence of integrated local NVMe storage and high-end hardware acceleration makes it best suited for scalable stateless services, continuous integration build jobs, Redis caching layers, and multi-threaded background task processing where parallel execution compensates for older architectural single-thread clock limitations.
description: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sn1ne.4xlarge is a compute-optimized virtual machine featuring 16 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, running on the KVM hypervisor with an x86_64 Intel Xeon E5-2682v4 processor clocked at 2.5 GHz. Configured with a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the hardware includes 35 MB of L3 cache, baseline networking of 3 Gbps, and no local disk storage or GPU acceleration. Benchmarks show modest single-thread execution, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 930.0, but stable parallel processing, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 13034.32 and multi-threaded decompression throughput of 57.0 GB/sec. The instance delivers cost-effective core density for workloads that scale across threads, making it suitable for CI/CD compilation pipelines, distributed caching engines like Redis, multi-threaded batch jobs, and general compute-bound web tier services.
